hero.title: Frequently asked questions
hero.summary: Find answers about generation, quality, history, and your account — organized by topic and fully searchable.

no_results: No answer matched the current query. Try another keyword or switch categories.

getting-started.q1: What should I do before the first run?
getting-started.a1: Start with a focused prompt, keep the subject and lighting explicit, and avoid stacking too many stylistic requests at once.
getting-started.q2: When should I use a reference image?
getting-started.a2: Add one when pose, framing, or lighting needs to stay anchored. It is usually better than over-describing those constraints in text.

quality.q1: How do I improve output quality?
quality.a1: Raise steps carefully, keep the scene readable, and use negative guidance for distortion or clutter instead of padding the prompt with unrelated adjectives.
quality.q2: Why do similar prompts still vary?
quality.a2: The seed, model behavior, and system conditions can all shift the result. Save strong outputs to history and reuse their settings when you want consistency.

runtime.a1: Your request has been accepted but is still waiting for available system capacity. The generate page keeps that state visible until the engine begins rendering.
runtime.q2: What should I do after an error state?
runtime.a2: Retry with the same settings if the prompt is still valid, or reduce size and CFG if the system is failing under load.

history.a1: Yes. History supports prompt search, ratio filters, CFG bands, and a metadata table for scanning steps, seed, and timestamps.
history.a2: The visible archive depth follows your history limit setting, which can be adjusted from the settings control center.

account.q1: Why are login and recovery on different pages?
account.a1: The auth flow stays explicit so sign-in, recovery, and reset can each have their own states without collapsing into a single mixed-purpose screen.
account.q2: Where can I change interface behavior?
account.a2: Open Settings to control theme, accent, notifications, queue behavior, safety defaults, presets, density, and visual mode.
